title: How Systems Treat Intent: A Faceted Taxonomy of Intent for Human-AI Co-Creation
abstract: arXiv:2611.30793v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Human-AI interaction depends on systems acting on user intent rather than explicit procedures, even when that intent is incomplete, evolving, or partially communicable. Literature organizing systems by interaction technique, workflow stage, or division of labor, offer limited insight into which facet of intent an interaction mechanism addresses. We introduce a six-facet taxonomy of intent, grounded in philosophical accounts of mind, action, and meaning, and apply it to systems presented in 198 papers from eleven SIGCHI venues. Our analysis reveals that different forms of incomplete intent are associated with distinct interaction and authorship strategies, showing that mechanisms that appear similar often address fundamentally different intent-related problems. This exposes blind spots, as intent is rarely represented as an interaction object, authorship provenance is rarely tracked, and tentative preferences are rarely distinguished fr

translated_title: 系统如何对待意图：面向人机共创的多维度意图分类法
translated_abstract: 人机交互依赖于系统根据用户意图而非明确的操作步骤来采取行动，即使该意图是不完整的、不断演变的或只能部分传达的。现有文献按交互技术、工作流阶段或分工方式来组织系统，但对于某个交互机制究竟针对意图的哪个维度，所能提供的洞见有限。我们提出了一个包含六个维度的意图分类法，该分类法根植于关于心灵、行动与意义的哲学论述，并将其应用于来自十一个SIGCHI会议的198篇论文中所呈现的系统。我们的分析揭示，不同形式的不完整意图与不同的交互和创作归属策略相关联，这表明看似相似的机制往往解决的是根本不同的意图相关问题。这暴露了当前设计的盲点：意图很少被作为交互对象来呈现，创作归属来源很少被追踪，试探性的偏好很少被加以区分（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文提出了一个根植于哲学理论、涵盖六个维度的意图分类法，并通过对198篇SIGCHI论文中系统的分析，揭示了现有系统在处理不完整用户意图时普遍存在的设计盲点。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a philosophically grounded six-facet taxonomy of intent and, through an analysis of 198 SIGCHI papers, reveals blind spots in how current systems address incomplete user intent in human-AI co-creation.
